title: Death Toll Reaches Three in Delhi's Seemapuri Building Collapse
excerpt: A pregnant woman and two children are among the dead after the front of a four-storey building near Idgah Machhli Mandi collapsed Wednesday afternoon; eleven were rescued and an inquiry into the cause is underway.
body:
• The death toll from Wednesday's building collapse in New Seemapuri, northeast Delhi, has risen to three: Gulafsa, 21, who was four months pregnant; a 12-year-old girl; and a child aged about one-and-a-half years.
  • Eleven people have been rescued from the debris, eight of them injured and moved to Rajiv Gandhi Super Speciality Hospital in Tahirpur.
  • The front portion of the four-storey building came down around 3:30 pm near Idgah Machhli Mandi; fire, police, disaster-response and civic agencies worked into the night, alongside residents digging with bare hands.
  • Neighbours say cracks appeared in the structure after Tuesday-night tremors from an earthquake in Uttarakhand; the official cause is under investigation.

Three people are dead after a four-storey residential building collapsed in northeast Delhi's New Seemapuri on Wednesday afternoon, officials confirmed, as rescue teams pulled a final count of eleven survivors from the rubble. The victims include a 21-year-old woman who was four months pregnant and two children, aged 12 and about one-and-a-half years.

The front portion of the building, near Idgah Machhli Mandi, came crashing down around 3:30 pm. The Delhi Fire Services received the first call within minutes, and teams from the Delhi Police, the Delhi Disaster Management Authority, the National Disaster Response Force, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) and the Delhi Urban Shelter Improvement Board (DUSIB) converged on the site with excavators and ambulances, working through the evening.

"Eleven people have been rescued from the debris so far, including eight injured persons who have been shifted to the Rajiv Gandhi Super Speciality Hospital, Tahirpur. The operation is ongoing."

— Delhi Police officer, to PTI

The eight injured were identified as Momin Mirja, 56, Abdaan, 3, Abdul Rehman, 28, Devruddin, 28, Salma, 50, Chote, 34, Sakina, 35, and Samad, 30. All were taken to Rajiv Gandhi Super Speciality Hospital in Tahirpur. Initial agency counts varied as the rescue unfolded; earlier in the afternoon, Shahdara DCP Rajendra Prasad Meena said seven people had been rescued and were out of danger.

Residents were among the first on the rubble. Videos from the site showed people clearing bricks by hand and carrying a rescued woman to safety. One resident told reporters that police reached the spot about half an hour after the collapse and that locals had already pulled several people out.

A structure already showing stress

Authorities have not pinned down a cause, but neighbours told officials the building had developed visible cracks after tremors from an earthquake in Uttarakhand shook Delhi-NCR on Tuesday night. The MCD said the owner was in the process of vacating the building. The civic body described the structure as roughly 20 to 25 years old and standing on a plot of about 225 square feet in a jhuggi-jhopri cluster, though police and a local councillor gave different estimates of its age and size — a reminder of how little reliable documentation exists for housing in such settlements.

https://x.com/ANI/status/2107954598631948460

Local accounts say families engaged in ragpicking lived in the building and that some people were collecting plastic and other material when the structure gave way. The collapse also brought down walls of an adjoining building and the boundary wall of a nearby mosque.

Impact: a familiar, unresolved failure

The collapse is the second deadly building failure in the capital in a month. On September 6, a five-storey paying-guest building in southwest Delhi's Satya Niketan collapsed, killing seven people and injuring 12; police detained the building's owner among five people. After that incident, the MCD said it would act against unsafe structures — a promise the Seemapuri collapse puts under fresh scrutiny.

Delhi's monsoon season routinely weakens aging structures, and experts have long warned that buildings in dense, low-income clusters often lack both structural audits and any clear line of accountability between landlords, tenants and civic bodies. When a structure is occupied while being vacated, as here, evacuation authority becomes blurred — nobody is clearly responsible for keeping people out of a failing building.

"We received information at 3:40 PM. This is a four-storey building, which is 25 square yards in area. All agencies are present at the scene; ambulances and Delhi Fire Service staff are deployed."

— Rajendra Prasad Meena, DCP Shahdara, to ANI

What's next

Rescue teams were still clearing debris late Wednesday in search of anyone who might remain trapped. The Delhi Traffic Police advised commuters to avoid the Seemapuri area, with movement affected around Seemapuri Gol Chakkar, DLF Bhopura and adjoining roads, and asked the public not to stop or gather near the site so ambulances and rescue vehicles could move through.

Officials said a formal investigation would determine whether the Tuesday tremors, construction quality, or both caused the collapse. The inquiry's findings — and whether the MCD moves against the unsafe structures it identified after Satya Niketan — will show whether this tragedy changes anything on the ground.
